title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-03-30
lineage: AUD > MR > D > PCM > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Surprisingly clear ’68 audience tape delivers a scorching set with The Other One, Dark Star and the rare Born Cross‑Eyed → Spanish Jam sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording—an AUD source from March 1968—holds up better than most early tapes, offering crisp enough sound to enjoy the band’s high‑energy playing. Highlights include a fiery The Other One, an expansive Dark Star, a rare Born Cross‑Eyed into Spanish Jam, and the classic China Cat → Eleven transition, though Lovelight loses momentum partway through. Overall the show is regarded as one of the era’s stronger performances despite occasional mix quirks.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating from 18 reviews is ~4.1; most reviewers praise both music and tape quality, with only a few negative outliers.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners note surprisingly clear sound for a 1968 AUD, with occasional murkiness and a source switch around the Dancin' segment; Pigpen's keyboard is muted on some parts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong, jam‑heavy second half with rare song pairings; a few transitions (e.g., China Cat into Eleven) are noted as less smooth, but overall pacing keeps the energy high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's lead work is repeatedly praised, especially his solos in Dark Star and The Other One; also highlighted for engaging banter that gets the crowd shouting suggestions.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s keyboard often muted, noted as a drawback to the 1968 sound.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard presence uneven—Pigpen's parts missing on some sections.
